Roping in a cyclone occurs when the underflow discharge from the spigot collapses into a solid stream instead of a hollow cone, indicating a lack of air core. This happens when the spigot is too small, preventing the air core from forming, or too large, allowing too much water to leave. The correct flare angle is 30 to 40 degrees, and the spigot size should match the amount of feed to the cyclone to maintain an air core and prevent roping [1][2].
